subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Trust
overview: To trust means to depend on someone because you believe they will not let you down. In this sub-strand you will learn how Joseph stayed faithful to God and to his master when Potiphar's wife tempted him, how to say No firmly to temptations and to strangers, which people you can trust for your safety, and why Christians put their trust in God always, as Psalm 125:1 teaches.

lessons.title: Joseph and Potiphar's wife
objectives: Retell the story of Joseph and Potiphar's wife from Genesis 39:7-12.
List lessons learnt from the story.
Explain how young people can copy Joseph by keeping away from sexual temptations.
lessons.intro: Have you ever been asked to do something you knew was wrong, and the person kept asking again and again? Joseph faced this in Egypt. His answer and his action are a good example for every young Christian.
lessons.notes:
### Who was Joseph?
Joseph was a son of Jacob. His jealous brothers sold him, and he was taken to Egypt. There he was bought by Potiphar, one of the king's officers. The Bible says the LORD was with Joseph and made everything he did succeed. Potiphar saw this, trusted Joseph and put him in charge of his whole house.

### The story (Genesis 39:7-12)
- Joseph was a young, good-looking man. After some time, Potiphar's wife began to desire him and asked him to sleep with her. This was a sexual temptation.
- Joseph refused. He told her that his master had trusted him with everything in the house except her, because she was his master's wife.
- Joseph asked, "How then could I do such an immoral thing and sin against God?"
- She kept asking him day after day, but he would not listen to her and kept away from her.
- One day Joseph went into the house to do his work and none of the servants was there. She caught him by his robe and asked him again.
- Joseph did not stay to argue. He escaped and ran outside, leaving his robe in her hand.

Later in the chapter she told lies about Joseph and he was put in prison, but the Bible says the LORD was with Joseph there too (Genesis 39:20-21).

### Lessons from the story
- Joseph was faithful to God. He saw the wrong act as sin against God, not only against Potiphar.
- Joseph was trustworthy. He did not betray the master who trusted him.
- He said No clearly, and he kept saying No every time.
- He ran away from the tempting place. Running away from temptation is wise, not cowardly.
- Doing right can sometimes bring trouble, but God stays with those who obey Him.

### Copying Joseph today
Young people may be tempted by someone who touches them badly, asks them to go to a hidden place, shows them bad pictures or offers gifts in exchange for wrong acts. Like Joseph, you can refuse, move away quickly and tell a trusted adult.

keyWords.meaning: something that pulls you towards doing wrong
being pushed or invited into wrong touching or sexual acts
a person others can depend on to do right

activity.title: Reading and retelling Genesis 39:7-12
materials: Good News Bible or Children's Bible
steps: In turns, read Genesis 39:7-12 aloud, one verse per learner.
Close the Bible and, as a group, retell the story in the correct order.
List on the board the lessons learnt from the story of Joseph and Potiphar's wife.
Each learner writes one way he or she will copy Joseph.

practice.question: In whose house did Joseph work in Egypt?
practice.answer: In the house of Potiphar, one of the king's officers.

practice.question: What did Joseph say when Potiphar's wife tempted him?
practice.answer: He refused and asked how he could do such an immoral thing and sin against God.

practice.question: What did Joseph do when she caught him by his robe?
practice.answer: He escaped and ran outside, leaving his robe in her hand.

practice.question: Give two lessons we learn from Joseph.
practice.answer: Any two: be faithful to God; be trustworthy; say No clearly; run away from temptation; God is with those who obey Him.

summary: Joseph refused Potiphar's wife because doing wrong would be sin against God.
He kept saying No and ran away from temptation.
Young Christians should copy Joseph by keeping away from sexual temptations.

lessons.title: Saying No and people we can trust
objectives: Say No firmly to tempting situations and to strangers.
Name people they can trust at home, at school and in the community.
State whom to report to when in danger.
lessons.intro: A stranger stops you on your way home from school and offers you sweets and a ride. What should you do? Knowing how to say No, and knowing whom to run to, can keep you safe.
lessons.notes:
### Being assertive
To be assertive means to say clearly and respectfully what you want and what you will not do. An assertive child does not give in just because someone is older, kind, or keeps asking.

Ways to say No firmly:
- Look at the person and say "No!" in a strong, clear voice.
- Do not give long explanations or argue.
- Walk or run away to a safe place where there are people you trust.
- Tell a trusted adult as soon as possible, even if the person told you to keep it a secret.

### Tempting and dangerous situations
- A stranger offers you gifts, money, sweets or a lift.
- Someone asks you to go with them to a lonely or hidden place.
- Someone touches you in a way that makes you uncomfortable, or asks you to keep touching a secret.
- Someone shows you bad pictures or videos.

You can avoid many of these by walking in groups, going straight home after school, not staying in lonely places, and not accepting gifts from people you do not know.

### People you can trust
People we can trust are those who care for us and want us to be safe:
- At home: parents, guardians, grandparents, older brothers and sisters who care for you.
- At school: the class teacher, the head teacher, the school nurse.
- In the community: church leaders, Sunday school teachers, police officers, chiefs, and a trusted neighbour your parents know.

Sometimes even a person we know can try to harm us. If anyone, a stranger or a relative, makes you feel unsafe, say No and tell another person you trust.

### Whom to report to when in danger
Report to a parent, guardian, teacher or police officer. In Kenya, children can also call Childline Kenya on 116 free of charge, or the police on 999 or 112.

keyWords.meaning: able to say clearly and politely what you will or will not do
a person you do not know
to tell a responsible person what has happened

examples.problem: Wanjiku is walking home when a man she does not know says, "Your mother sent me to pick you. Get into my car." What should she do?
steps: She does not know the man, so he is a stranger.
Her parents never told her someone would pick her.
She should say No firmly, move away to where there are people she trusts, and tell her parent or teacher.
examples.answer: Say No, do not get into the car, run to a safe place and report to a trusted adult.

activity.title: Role-play: Saying No!
steps: In pairs, one learner acts as a stranger offering sweets or a lift; the other says "No!" firmly and walks away.
Swap roles and practise saying No to someone who invites you to a hidden place.
In groups, list the people you can trust at home, school and in the community, and discuss whom to report to when in danger.
Write a short poem titled 'People I trust' and read it to the class.

practice.question: What does it mean to be assertive?
practice.answer: To say clearly and respectfully what you will or will not do, without giving in.

practice.question: Name two people you can trust at school.
practice.answer: Any two, for example the class teacher, the head teacher, the school nurse.

practice.question: Why should you avoid talking to strangers?
practice.answer: Some strangers may want to harm, abuse or kidnap children, so talking to them or going with them is dangerous.

practice.question: What number can a child in Kenya call free to get help?

summary: Say No firmly, move away and tell a trusted adult.
Trusted people include parents, guardians, teachers, church leaders and police officers.
Report danger even if someone tells you to keep it a secret.

lessons.title: Trusting in God: Psalm 125:1
objectives: List reasons why Christians should trust God.
Show trust in God in daily life.
lessons.intro: People can sometimes disappoint us. A friend may forget a promise. But the Bible teaches that God never fails those who depend on Him.
lessons.notes:
### What is trusting God?
To trust God means to depend on Him completely in everything we do. We believe that He loves us, hears our prayers, and is able to help us.

### Psalm 125:1
The Good News Bible says:

"Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which can never be shaken, never be moved."

Mount Zion was the hill in Jerusalem where the Temple stood. A mountain is strong. Wind and rain do not move it. The psalm teaches that a person who trusts God stays strong and steady like that mountain, even when troubles come.

### Why should we trust God?
- God created everything and is in control of all things.
- God loves us and cares for us as a father cares for his children.
- God is always with us, at home, at school and on the way.
- God keeps His promises and never fails.
- When we trust God we are not overcome by fear or worry.
- Joseph trusted God in Egypt, and God was with him in Potiphar's house and even in prison.

### How we show trust in God
- Praying about everything: exams, sickness, safety, needs at home.
- Obeying God's word even when others do wrong.
- Thanking God in good and hard times.
- Asking God for help instead of turning to wrong ways, such as cheating in an examination.
- Singing songs of trust, such as choruses and hymns sung in church.

Trusting God does not mean we stop being careful. We trust God and we also obey the safety rules our parents and teachers give us.

keyWords.meaning: the hill in Jerusalem where the Temple stood

activity.title: Reciting and singing about trust
steps: Read Psalm 125:1 together, then write it on a flash card.
Recite the verse in pairs until each learner can say it without looking.
As a class, list the importance of trusting God on the board.
Sing a song you know about trusting God.

practice.question: Recite Psalm 125:1.
practice.answer: Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which can never be shaken, never be moved.

practice.question: In Psalm 125:1, what are people who trust God compared to?
practice.answer: Mount Zion, which can never be shaken or moved.

practice.question: Give three reasons why Christians should trust God.
practice.answer: Any three: He created and controls everything; He loves and cares for us; He is always with us; He keeps His promises; trusting Him removes fear.

summary: Trusting God means depending on Him completely.
Psalm 125:1: those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, never shaken.
We show trust by praying, obeying and thanking God always.

quiz.question: Which Bible passage tells the story of Joseph and Potiphar's wife?
Why did Joseph refuse Potiphar's wife?
options: He was afraid of the servants
He did not want to sin against God and betray his master
He wanted to go back home
quiz.explanation: Joseph asked how he could do such an immoral thing and sin against God.

quiz.question: What did Joseph leave in the hand of Potiphar's wife when he ran away?
quiz.explanation: Genesis 39:12 says he escaped and ran outside, leaving his robe in her hand.

quiz.question: What is the best thing to do when someone tempts you to do a wrong act?
options: Say No firmly, move away and tell a trusted adult
quiz.explanation: Being assertive means saying No clearly, leaving and reporting.

quiz.question: A stranger offers you sweets and asks you to follow him. What should you do?
quiz.answer: Say No, do not take the sweets, go to a safe place and tell a parent, teacher or other trusted adult.
quiz.explanation: Strangers may want to harm or kidnap children.

quiz.question: Which of these is a person you can trust at school?
options: A person selling sweets outside the fence
quiz.explanation: Teachers are responsible for learners' safety at school.

quiz.question: Name two people in the community you can report to when in danger.
quiz.answer: Any two, for example a police officer, a chief, a church leader, a trusted neighbour.
quiz.explanation: These are responsible people who can help keep children safe.

quiz.question: What should you do if a relative touches you in a bad way and tells you to keep it secret?
quiz.explanation: Anyone who harms you should be reported, even a relative.

quiz.question: Complete Psalm 125:1: "Those who trust in the LORD are like ______."
quiz.explanation: The verse compares them to Mount Zion, which can never be shaken.

quiz.question: Give one reason why we should put our trust in God.
quiz.answer: Any one: He created and controls everything; He loves us; He is always with us; He never fails.
quiz.explanation: God is faithful and able to help.
